# Case 3: `jaxdft`

I tried to build something substantial with `claude code`, my idea was a `jax`-based DFT code
with the explicit purpose of being able to run on GPU.

## The project

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="60%"}
A GPU-first plane-wave DFT code in JAX, with two goals, in this order:

1. Explore building a substantial scientific code through agentic development.
2. Produce real, verifiable physics along the way.

Built so far: band structures, self-consistent LDA, k-point sampling, forces from `jax.grad`,
runs on CPU clusters and V100 GPUs.

[Everything is public: [mads-peter.com/jaxdft](https://mads-peter.com/jaxdft/)]{.muted .compact}
:::

::: {.column width="40%"}
::: {.compact}
[9 days]{.accent style="font-size:2.2em; font-weight:700; line-height:1"}\
5–13 November, 73 commits

[4.1k / 8.0k]{.accent-strong style="font-size:2.2em; font-weight:700; line-height:1"}\
lines of package / lines of tests

[14k]{.accent-strong style="font-size:2.2em; font-weight:700; line-height:1"}\
lines of Quarto: theory, validation, logs
:::
:::
::::

::: notes
70 of the 73 commits are co-authored by Claude. Twice as many lines of tests as of code.
The site has sections for theory, concepts, ideas, validation, engineering and research
logs, and excerpts of the development conversations.

## Validated, milestone by milestone

::: {.compact .wide}
| Milestone | Physics | Checked against | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1a | Empty-lattice bands, fcc | Analytic free-electron bands | Bit-for-bit identical |
| 1b | Silicon, Cohen–Bergstresser pseudopotential | Published levels (1966) | Within 0.089 eV |
| 2a | Self-consistent LDA for H₂; forces from autodiff | DFTK, same discrete problem | Within 3 × 10⁻¹¹ a.u. |
| 2b | Self-consistent LDA silicon, k-points, nonlocal projectors | DFTK, same discrete problem | Within 3 × 10⁻¹¹ a.u. |
| 2c | Eigensolver for large k-grids and GPUs | The 2b code: same energies | 8³ k-grid on a V100: 40 s → 6.1 s |
:::

::: {.wide}
[Every number is computed by a validation document each time the site is built. A document that disagrees with the code fails the build.]{.muted}
:::

::: notes
The validation ladder from CLAUDE.md: analytic limits first, then published numbers,
then reference codes run on the same system.
The 2b LDA gap is 0.47 eV against 1.17 eV in experiment; that is the known LDA
underestimate, not an error, which is why the table compares with DFTK instead.
:::

## The loop, in the git log

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="62%"}
::: {.compact}
| Step | Commit (Milestone 1b, all on 5 November) |
|---|---|
| Spec | draft theory post for Cohen–Bergstresser silicon |
| | theory post: incorporate Cohen–Bergstresser 1966 details |
| Review | revise theory post after review |
| | record agreed API; update pseudopotential protocol in CLAUDE.md |
| Tests | acceptance, property and unit tests (failing, pre-implementation) |
| Implement | implement Structure, units, Cohen–Bergstresser and LocalPotential |
| Validate | validation document, matrix-element direction test, logs |
:::
:::

::: {.column width="38%"}
> "Do not write or change acceptance tests to fit an implementation. If a test looks wrong, stop and raise it."

[From the project's `CLAUDE.md`]{.muted .compact}
:::
::::

::: notes
Every milestone has the same sequence of commits. The theory post is reviewed by me,
and for several milestones also by a second model outside the session.
The API is agreed through rounds of questions before the acceptance tests are written,
so the tests can be committed failing.
:::

## What the tests couldn't catch

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
After milestone 2a, reading the code:

> "The mixing scheme is hardcoded, the class describes the parameters but not the method."

> "Can you check if there are other places where such abstractions are missing? If you find any propose them before changing any code."
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
::: {.compact}
- `CLAUDE.md` already asked for algorithms behind abstractions. The agent hard-coded the mixing anyway.
- The fix: a `Mixer` protocol. Results **bitwise identical** before and after.
- The audit found six more places; three changed now, three left for the milestones that need them.
- Every test passed throughout. **Tests check behaviour, not architecture.**
:::
:::
::::

::: notes
The three changes: SCF terms found by role instead of by class name (it required a class
literally named "Ewald"), the preconditioner as an option, and the initial density as an option.
Source: the "Missing abstraction" conversation excerpt and the engineering log, 6 November.
:::

## How it went

[It worked. Review is the cost.]{.accent style="font-size:1.4em; font-weight:700"}

::: {.compact .wide}
- **Worked:** five milestones of validated physics in nine days, agreeing with a production code to 10⁻¹¹.
- **The bottleneck was me:** reading theory posts, tests and code at every gate.
- **Review needs material:** theory posts, failing tests and validation documents are what made the agent's work reviewable.
:::

[N = 1, my own project, my own judgement.]{.muted}
